source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Analyze the inspection records carefully, noting any anomalies or violations. Record dates, locations, specific water quality parameters that failed (such as pH, turbidity, E. coli levels, etc.), and the acceptable range. 

3. Verify the test results.
Conduct another test to confirm the results using a different test kit or instrument to ensure the accuracy of the initial findings. Document the methods of verification and any new data collected. 

4. Compare with past data.
Review past water-quality test results of the same water source to identify any patterns or recurring issues. This helps determine if the failure is an isolated incident or part of a larger, ongoing problem.

5. Notify relevant authorities.
Report the findings immediately to the local water utility, environmental protection agency, and public health department. Provide all collected data and analysis. 

6. Initiate public notification.
Work with local health departments, emergency management agencies, and communication teams to notify the public promptly.
